title: Supervision of Fire Alarm Systems
page_numbering: PDF page index (1 = first page of the PDF file)

questions.question: If no FLS Director or F-80 holder is required, which Certificate of Fitness must supervise an approved fire alarm system WITHOUT a voice communication system?
questions.explanation: Any approved fire alarm system without voice communication (no FLSD/F-80 required) must be supervised by an S-95 holder.

source.quote: any approved fire alarm system without voice communication system must be under supervision of an S-95 Certificate of Fitness holder.

questions.question: Which Certificate of Fitness holders are exempt from obtaining a separate S-95 for the same premises?
questions.explanation: Holders of F-89/T-89/F-80/F-53 are exempt from a separate S-95 for the same premises.

source.quote: The individuals who have obtained the F-89/T-89/F-80/F-53 Certificate of Fitness will be exempt from having to obtain a separate S-95

questions.question: What document should Certificate of Fitness holders make sure their premises' fire alarm system is approved by?
questions.explanation: COF holders should ensure the premises fire alarm system is approved by an FDNY letter of approval.

source.quote: All Certificate of Fitness holders should ensure their respective premises have fire alarm systems approved by a FDNY letter of approval.

questions.question: What does a supervisory signal indicate?
options: That a fire drill has ended
That the system has been reset
The need for action in connection with supervision of guard tours, fire extinguishing systems or related maintenance features
That a fire is definitely present
questions.explanation: A supervisory signal indicates the need for action related to supervision of systems or maintenance features.

source.quote: SUPERVISORY SIGNAL: A signal indicating the need for action in connection with the supervision of guard tours, fire extinguishing systems or equipment

questions.question: What does a trouble signal indicate?
options: That a sprinkler is flowing water
A fault in a monitored circuit or component
questions.explanation: A trouble signal indicates a fault in a monitored circuit or component and must be investigated and corrected by an approved company.

source.quote: TROUBLE SIGNAL: A signal initiated by the fire alarm system or device indicative of a fault in a monitored circuit or component.

questions.question: The fire alarm system functions as designed, but the alarm was caused by cigarette smoke in a non-smoking area. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: An unnecessary alarm is one where the system worked as designed but an FDNY response proved unnecessary, such as cigarette smoke.

source.quote: An example of an unnecessary alarm is an alarm triggered by smoke from a lit cigarette in a non-smoking area

questions.question: An alarm caused by improper smoke detector placement is an example of:
questions.explanation: Unwarranted alarms result when the system fails to function as designed, e.g., improper detector placement.

source.quote: Examples of unwarranted alarms are alarms resulting from improper smoke detector placement, improper detector setting for installed location

questions.question: What feature reduces the number of unwarranted alarms?
questions.explanation: The alarm verification feature reduces the number of unwarranted alarms.

source.quote: It is important to know that the alarm verification feature reduces the number of unwarranted alarms.

questions.question: In the study material, what does the word "SHALL" indicate?
options: A suggestion for large buildings only
questions.explanation: SHALL indicates a mandatory requirement; SHOULD indicates a recommendation.

source.quote: SHALL. Indicates a mandatory requirement.

questions.question: May an S-95 Certificate of Fitness holder perform smoke detector cleaning?
options: Yes, if the detector is analog
questions.explanation: S-95 holders are not allowed to perform smoke detector cleaning; it must be done by a properly certified person.

source.quote: The S-95 Certificate of Fitness holders are not allowed to perform the smoke detector cleaning.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of fire alarm systems within protected premises?
options: To warn building occupants and transmit fire signals to the Fire Department via an approved central station
questions.explanation: The primary purpose is to warn occupants and transmit fire signals to the FDNY via an FDNY-approved central station company.

source.quote: THE PRIMARY PURPOSE OF FIRE ALARM SYSTEMS WITHIN PROTECTED PREMISES IS TO WARN BUILDING OCCUPANTS AND TRANSMIT SIGNALS INDICATING A FIRE CONDITION

questions.question: Is it lawful to install a security camera disguised as a smoke detector that does not perform a fire protection function?
options: Yes, if a real detector is within 10 feet
No; non-functioning devices resembling fire protection equipment are never permitted
questions.explanation: It is unlawful to install or maintain any fire protection device that does not perform the fire protection function.

source.quote: It is unlawful to install or maintain any fire protection device which does not perform the fire protection function.

questions.question: In what order must central station operators process fire alarm signals?
options: In the order they are received
Before any other signals, regardless of the order received
questions.explanation: Fire alarm signals are processed before all other signals regardless of the order received.

source.quote: Central station operators must monitor and process all fire alarm signals before any other signals, regardless of the order in which they are received.

questions.question: A fire alarm signal is automatically restored by the premises system. Must the central station still retransmit it to the FDNY?
options: Yes; every fire alarm signal must be retransmitted, with no exceptions
questions.explanation: Every fire alarm signal must be retransmitted immediately, even if automatically restored. There are no exceptions.

source.quote: EVERY fire alarm signal must be re-transmitted immediately to the FDNY as a fire alarm signal even if it is automatically restored

questions.question: Which device generates a SUPERVISORY signal?
options: Low air pressure switch on a dry pipe sprinkler system
questions.explanation: Supervisory signals come from devices like valve supervisory switches, tank level switches, dry-pipe low air switches and fire pump monitors.

source.quote: 3. Low air pressure switch from a dry pipe sprinkler system

questions.question: Which of the following is a common trouble condition monitored by a FACP?
options: Water flowing in a sprinkler pipe
questions.explanation: Common trouble conditions include battery condition, AC failure, ground fault, open or short circuits, phone line failure and internal component failure.

source.quote: conditions monitored by a FACP are battery condition, AC failure, ground fault, open or short circuit on a wire, phone line failure

questions.question: Routine handling of a trouble signal by the central station should take a maximum of how long until the telephone investigation begins?
questions.explanation: Routine handling should take a maximum of four minutes from receipt to initiation of investigation by telephone.

source.quote: Routine handling should take a maximum of four minutes from receipt of a trouble signal by the central station

questions.question: How must a sub-system (e.g., range hood, FM200, pre-action) relate to the base building fire alarm system?
options: It must report directly to tenants
It must only connect to the elevator
It must be interconnected to it for alarm and trouble supervision
questions.explanation: All sub-systems must be interconnected to the base building fire alarm system and annunciate their type and location.

source.quote: All sub-systems must be interconnected to the base building fire alarm system for alarm and trouble supervision

questions.question: After an alarm, what must the S-95 holder record in the log book?
options: Only the time the alarm stopped
Date and time, location, which device was activated, and the probable cause
questions.explanation: The S-95 holder records the date and time of the alarm, its location, the activated device and the probable cause.

source.quote: The S-95 COF holder must record the date and time of alarm, its location, which device was the activated, and the probable cause.

questions.question: Does pressing the alarm silence switch stop the signal from being transmitted to the central station?
questions.explanation: The silence switch does not prevent a signal from being transmitted to the central station.

source.quote: the silence switch does not prevent a signal from being transmitted to a FDNY approved central station company.

questions.question: When may the fire alarm system be reset after an alarm?
options: As soon as the alarm noise stops
Only after the condition is verified by FDNY personnel
questions.explanation: Never reset the fire alarm system until the condition is verified by FDNY personnel.

source.quote: Never reset the fire alarm system until the condition is verified by the FDNY personnel.

questions.question: After a fire alarm is reset, what usually needs to be done for fans?
options: Restart them from a separate "fan restart" button or key switch
Call the central station to restart them
questions.explanation: After reset, the fan usually requires restarting from a separate fan restart button or key switch.

source.quote: After a fire alarm is reset, the fan usually requires restarting from a separate “fan restart” button or key switch.

questions.question: What normally happens to a fixed-temperature heat detector after it sounds an alarm?
options: It is moved to another room
questions.explanation: Fixed-temperature heat detectors normally require replacement after alarming (intelligent ones usually reset).

source.quote: The fixed-temperature heat detectors normally require replacement after they have sounded an alarm.

questions.question: Which heat detector is more sensitive?
questions.explanation: The rate-of-rise detector is more sensitive than the fixed temperature detector.

source.quote: This type of detector is more sensitive than the fixed temperature detector.

questions.question: A carbon monoxide detector activates. What must happen before the panel can be reset?
options: The S-95 holder opens a window
The FDNY must determine carbon monoxide is at safe levels
The central station resets it remotely
questions.explanation: For a CO detector, FDNY must determine CO at safe levels in the space before the panel can be reset.

source.quote: FDNY must determine carbon monoxide at safe levels in space before panel can be reset.

questions.question: How often must smoke detectors connected to a defined fire alarm system be cleaned (non-analog)?
options: Not less than once every six months
questions.explanation: Smoke detectors must be cleaned not less than once every six months; analog detectors within one week of a cleaning indication.

source.quote: cleaned not less than once every six (6) months, except for analog (intelligent) smoke detectors

questions.question: How often must smoke detectors be tested for smoke entry?
options: Not less than once a year
questions.explanation: Smoke detectors must be tested for smoke entry not less than once a year.

source.quote: tested for smoke entry not less than once a year.

questions.question: An analog (intelligent) smoke detector indicates it needs cleaning. Within what time must it be cleaned?
questions.explanation: Analog smoke detectors must be cleaned no later than one week from receipt of an indication of the need for cleaning.

source.quote: except for analog (intelligent) smoke detectors, which must be cleaned no later than one (1) week from receipt of an indication

questions.question: Which building function does the fire alarm system commonly control during an alarm?
options: Recall of elevator cars to a designated landing floor
questions.explanation: The fire alarm system integrates with elevator controls to recall elevator cars to a designated landing floor.

source.quote: The fire alarm system integrates with elevator controls to recall elevator cars to a designated landing floor in the event of an alarm.

questions.question: How do smoke detectors compare to heat detectors in detecting most fires?
options: Smoke detectors detect most fires much more rapidly
Smoke detectors only work on Class D fires
questions.explanation: Smoke detectors detect most fires much more rapidly than heat detectors.

source.quote: Smoke detectors detect most fires much more rapidly than heat detectors.

questions.question: During construction, when should listed smoke detector covers be removed?
options: Only at the end of the project
At the end of each shift or when work stops
questions.explanation: Cover detectors only during dust-generating work; remove covers at the end of each shift or when work stops.

source.quote: Remove covers at the end of each shift or when work stops.

questions.question: Does a sprinkler waterflow alarm-initiating device turn the water on or off?
options: Yes, it turns the water off
No; it only detects flow and sends an alarm signal
Yes, it turns the water on
questions.explanation: The waterflow device detects flow and sends a signal; it does not turn water on or off.

source.quote: This device does not turn on or off the water.

questions.question: Carbon monoxide detectors are required in any building that has what?
options: Fossil fuel (gas or oil) burning equipment
questions.explanation: CO detectors are required in any building with fossil (gas and oil) fuel burning equipment.

source.quote: Carbon monoxide detectors are required in any building that has fossil (gas and oil) fuel burning equipment.

questions.question: If a flammable gas detector is connected to the FACP, what signal does its activation generate?
options: A fire alarm signal with building tones
A trouble signal only at the detector
questions.explanation: Gas detector activation on the FACP generates a supervisory signal transmitted to the central station; no alarm tone sounds on premises.

source.quote: the activation will generate a supervisory signal on the Fire Alarm Control Panel and be transmitted to the Central Station.

questions.question: It is unlawful to transmit how many unnecessary or unwarranted alarms in any three-month period?
questions.explanation: It is unlawful to transmit two or more unnecessary or unwarranted alarms in any three-month period.

source.quote: It is unlawful to transmit two (2) or more unnecessary or unwarranted alarms in any three-month period.

questions.question: Is a malicious false alarm from a manual fire alarm box considered an unnecessary alarm?
questions.explanation: The malicious transmission of a false alarm by a manual fire alarm box will not be considered an unnecessary alarm.

source.quote: The malicious transmission of a false alarm by activation of a manual fire alarm box will not be considered an unnecessary alarm.

questions.question: The partial/staged evacuation signal activates audio/visual devices on which floors?
options: The floor of alarm, the floor immediately above and the floor below
questions.explanation: Partial/staged signals activate devices on the floor of alarm plus the floor above and below; total/general activates all floors.

source.quote: activates the audio/visual devices only on the floor of alarm as well as the floor immediately above and the floor below.

questions.question: What does a two-way voice communication system use?
questions.explanation: Two-way voice communication uses warden phones, usually located near exit stairways, plus one at the FACP.

source.quote: Two-way voice communication system uses warden phones.

questions.question: A central station transmitter must have what?
options: A primary and secondary means of communication
questions.explanation: The central station transmitter must have a primary and secondary means of communication.

source.quote: The Central Station transmitter must have a primary and secondary means of communication.

questions.question: Who is authorized to perform service and testing on fire alarm systems?
options: Only certified technicians holding S-97 or S-98
questions.explanation: Only S-97 or S-98 certified technicians may perform service and testing.

source.quote: Only certified technicians holding S-97 or S-98 Certificate of Fitness are authorized to perform service and testing on the fire alarm systems.

questions.question: Where must the alarm log book be maintained?
options: On the premises, at the building's main fire alarm control panel
At the central station company's office
questions.explanation: The alarm log book is maintained on the premises at the main fire alarm control panel.

source.quote: An alarm log book must be maintained on the premises, at the building's main fire alarm control panel.

questions.question: What type of book must the alarm log book be?
options: A bound book (not spiral bound) with consecutively numbered, lined pages
questions.explanation: It must be bound (other than spiral bound) with consecutively numbered and lined pages.

source.quote: The alarm log book must be a bound book (other than spiral bound) with consecutively numbered and lined pages.

questions.question: How must alarm log book entries be made?
questions.explanation: All entries must be made in ink and dated.

source.quote: All entries must be made in ink and dated.

questions.question: How long must alarm log books be retained?
options: Three years from the date of the last entry
questions.explanation: Log books are retained three years from the last entry, and a separate book is kept for each calendar year.

source.quote: Log books must be retained for a period of three (3) years from the date of the last entry.

questions.question: Into how many separate sections must the alarm log book be divided?
questions.explanation: Daily entries, system off-line entries, activated alarm entries and notification entries: four sections.

source.quote: The alarm log book must be divided into 4 separate sections as set forth below.

questions.question: According to the NYC Fire Code as stated in the study material, what color must manual fire alarm boxes be?
questions.explanation: Manual fire alarm boxes must be red in color.

source.quote: Based on the New York City Fire Code, manual fire alarm boxes must be red in color.

questions.question: Before activating a fire alarm system for a test, inspection or fire drill, what is mandatory?
options: Take the system off-line by notifying the FDNY-approved central station beforehand
questions.explanation: It is mandatory to take the system off-line by notifying the central station beforehand to prevent unnecessary FDNY dispatch.

source.quote: it is mandatory to take the system “off-line” by notifying the FDNY approved central station company monitoring the fire alarm beforehand

questions.question: Is it necessary to take the system off-line for speaker audibility tests?
options: Only if more than one floor is tested
questions.explanation: It is not necessary to take the system offline when speaker audibility tests are being conducted.

source.quote: It is not necessary to take the system offline when the speaker audibility tests are being conducted.

questions.question: A manual fire alarm box is found defective. What should the Certificate of Fitness holder do?
options: Remove the box and throw it away
Notify the supervisor and put a placard over the box indicating it is out of service
Ignore it until the annual test
questions.explanation: The COF holder must notify the supervisor and place an out-of-service placard over the defective box.

source.quote: A Certificate of Fitness holder must notify his/her supervisor and put a placard over the defective box indicating that device is out of service.

questions.question: In the absence of a specific designee, who is considered the Impairment Coordinator?
questions.explanation: If no one is specifically designated, the owner is considered the Impairment Coordinator.

source.quote: In the absence of a specific designee, the owner must be considered the Impairment Coordinator.

questions.question: Portable fire extinguishers are required within what distance of commercial cooking equipment?
questions.explanation: Portable fire extinguishers are required within 30 feet of commercial cooking equipment.

source.quote: Within 30 feet of commercial cooking equipment.
